key_insight: A differentiable Schwarz-coupled finite element solver separates thin near-wall layers from bulk transport, enabling inverse modeling with adjoint sensitivities and agentic AI optimization.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets high-Péclet-number transport problems where resolving steep boundary-layer gradients makes simulation and parameter estimation computationally expensive.
method: Use perturbation theory to formulate overlapping inner and outer transport subproblems coupled through Schwarz iterations.
Differentiate the coupled FEM solver for inverse optimization with governing equations and boundary conditions imposed as hard constraints.
Use LLM-guided updates or an AI agent that stages optimization and expands a functional basis under a prescribed admission policy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower computational cost than a single-domain formulation and greater agentic AI benefit for functional-basis unknowns than nodal fields, but provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: Agentic optimization benefits appear representation-dependent; basis selection and admission rules require careful implementation.
paper_title: Differentiable Schwarz-Coupled Solvers for Thin Boundary Layer Transport: Inverse Modeling via Agentic AI Optimization
